article_title: Looped Transformers Test a 2025 AI Safety Warning on Chain-of-Thought Monitoring in Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini

content_preview.title: Looped Transformers Test a 2025 AI Safety Warning on Chain-of-Thought Monitoring in Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini
content_preview.summary: Thinking Machines built a looped-transformer model that reasons more without writing it down, then ran its own tests against a 2025 warning that this could weaken chain-of-thought safety monitoring.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Background

Monitoring a reasoning model's chain of thought (CoT) — the text it generates while working through a problem before giving an answer — has become one of the AI industry's go-to oversight tools, precisely because standard transformer architectures force reasoning into the open. editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured Analysis piece (Background / Current situation / Implications) with facts clearly separated from editorial assessment. The Implications section explicitly draws the boundaries of Thinking Machines' own findings (helpful-only fine-tune used for the agentic test, RL trained at only 3 passes, no third-party replication) rather than overstating them.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 4 snapshots from disk after verifying sha256 integrity against manifest.json (all 4 matched; all 4 fetched 200 OK, no archive_fallback, suspicious_patterns null for all). (1) sources/2026-11/.../source-0.html.gz (thinkingmachines.ai/news/inkling-2-mini/, dated Nov 20, 2026) — every direct quote in the submission attributed to Thinking Machines is verbatim against this snapshot: the CoT-monitoring framing passage (lines ~144-145), '5.4B weight activations per token to account for looping', '48 layer applications per token from 24 stored layers', the middle-layer design rationale, '27 out of 28 different evaluations', the Think Fast quote ('the variable-loop model's no-CoT time horizon improved from 16 seconds at one pass to 37 seconds with three' matches the TL;DR paragraph verbatim; note the detailed Results section phrases this differently ('rises ... at three') but the submission's quote matches the TL;DR passage exactly, not a paraphrase), 'the time horizon is roughly flat', 'kept improving out to ten loops', the GPQA Diamond legibility quote (1,661 vs. 3,703 tokens), the CoT-Control-QA quotes ('poor control over their CoT', 'at most 0.1% of the time', 'unable to distinguish controllability'), the LinuxArena 'no clear trend' quote, and the RL-caveat quotes ('do not tell us what a model trained with RL at a higher pass count would learn...', 'A cleaner comparison would include every pass count in RL'). All verbatim, no hallucinated or paraphrased-as-quoted text found. Architecture facts (26.4B total / 3.4B active parameters, 24 layers in four six-layer blocks, two middle blocks run 3x, 4-bit NVFP4 / 8-bit MXFP8 final four layers, ~20GB memory) all confirmed. (2) sources/.../source-1.html.gz (arxiv.org/abs/2507.11473) — confirmed this is a real, independently-authored 2025 position paper ('Chain of Thought Monitorability: A New and Fragile Opportunity for AI Safety', submitted 15 Jul 2025, revised 7 Dec 2025). Counted the listed authors: exactly 41 (Tomek Korbak + 40 others, matching the page's own 'and 40 other authors' phrasing). The three quoted fragments ('AI systems that think in human language...', 'CoT monitorability may be fragile', 'that frontier model developers consider the impact of development decisions on CoT monitorability') are all verbatim from the abstract. The article's characterization of the paper's warning is accurate: it correctly frames CoT monitorability as a fragile *opportunity* with a recommendation for developers to consider impact, not an assertion that monitorability will definitely be lost -- matching the abstract's actual hedged framing, no overstatement found. (3) sources/.../source-2.html.gz (VentureBeat) — confirms Thinking Machines Lab is 'started and led by former OpenAI chief technology officer Mira Murati', confirms Inkling 2 Mini runs locally/offline on consumer hardware (headline and body), confirms 26.4B/3.4B parameter figures, confirms architecture details (first/last 6-layer blocks run once, middle 12 run three times, 48 layer applications), and independently restates the same Think Fast/legibility/LinuxArena monitorability results Thinking Machines reported -- consistent, no contradiction. (4) sources/.../source-3.html.gz (TechCrunch, published 11:04 AM PDT, July 15, 2026) — confirms Inkling (the first model) is a 975-billion-total-parameter, open-weight, mixture-of-experts model released 'Wednesday morning' the same day as the article (July 15, 2026), and confirms Thinking Machines was founded by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati. All claims attributed to this source check out. Independent-source count for the Analysis requirement: 3 of 4 (arxiv.org, venturebeat.com, techcrunch.com) are independent of the subject; only thinkingmachines.ai is the vendor's own page -- exceeds the 2-of-4 minimum.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No hallucinated quotes, no fabricated specifics, no misattribution found across any of the 4 sources. Every number (26.4B/3.4B parameters, 975B for the original Inkling, 41 paper authors, 16s/37s no-CoT horizon, 1,661/3,703 GPQA tokens, 0.1% controllability rate, 20% N-Hop Lookup baseline, 27/28 evaluations) traces to a verbatim or directly-confirmed statement in a cited snapshot. Absence claim checked: 'The cited sources for this article do not report any third-party replication of Thinking Machines' monitorability tests' -- confirmed true across all 4 snapshots; none mentions independent replication. Qualifier/caveat language in the lead and Implications section ('not yet', 'on the evidence the company has published', 'by Thinking Machines' own account') correctly preserves the self-reported, unreplicated nature of the monitorability findings rather than presenting them as settled.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and analytical throughout. The piece does not adopt Thinking Machines' promotional framing; it explicitly flags the narrow scope of the company's own tests (helpful-only fine-tune for the agentic test, RL only at 3 passes, self-assessment rather than independent verification) as the central tension of the Implications section.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate. The Herald's existing 2026-11-22 Inkling 2 Mini article (src/content/articles/2026-11/22-gemini-4-neon-and-inkling-2-mini-claim-near-frontier-scores-at-lower-cost-but-both-trail-on-some-cited-benchmarks.md) covers cost/benchmark comparisons between Gemini 4 Neon and Inkling 2 Mini (Vals Index, Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, AA-Omniscience) and does not mention chain-of-thought monitorability, the 2025 CoT monitorability position paper, or any of the Think Fast / N-Hop Lookup / CoT-Control-QA / LinuxArena monitorability experiments this submission covers. Searched all published articles for 'monitorability' and for the paper's arXiv ID (2507.11473); no prior Herald coverage of this paper or these experiments exists. The angle is genuinely distinct from the Nov 22 piece -- confirmed.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Analysis requirements verified: 1,152 words (within 800-2000), 4 sources with 3 of 4 independent of the subject (arXiv paper, VentureBeat, TechCrunch independent; thinkingmachines.ai is the vendor's own page), examines a safety question across a release rather than merely recapping it, and keeps facts (Background/Current situation) separated from analysis (Implications). Every direct quote verified verbatim against the raw snapshot text; the 41-author count and the paper's fragile-opportunity framing are independently confirmed against the arXiv abstract itself, not a summary. Anthropic disclosure checked: the only 'Claude' string in the submission file is the contributor_model metadata field ('Claude Sonnet 5'); no Claude/Anthropic reference appears anywhere in the article body, title, or summary, so the disclosure rule does not apply. Originality confirmed against the Nov 22 Inkling 2 Mini cost/benchmark article -- no overlap. High-quality, well-sourced Analysis submission ready for publication as-is. Featured candidacy: 1 - a technically solid, well-verified safety-adjacent analysis for a defined AI-safety/developer audience; self-reported and unreplicated findings on a second-generation mini model keep it short of broad-audience significance.
